data.narrative:
Elroy Air, a Series B autonomous cargo drone company, is valued at $800M post-money and has raised $116M to date. The valuation landscape for frontier-stage drones and autonomous systems remains sparse; while eight private peers operate in the sector—including Zipline, Joby Aviation, Nuro, Archer Aviation, and Manna Aero—no public comparables exist. This fragmentation limits traditional peer-median benchmarking.

The valuation analysis relies on stage-progression methodology, the sole applicable triangulation method given insufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage peer clustering. Applying a typical Series B-to-next-stage step-up multiplier of 1.9x to the $800M last post-money valuation yields an implied value of $1.5B. A sensitivity band around this point estimate—accounting for variance in stage-specific growth expectations—ranges from $1.3B (low) to $1.7B (high).

The $1.5B median valuation reflects current market conditions for capital-intensive autonomous systems at Elroy's stage and fundraising trajectory. Primary uncertainties stem from the absence of closely-matched private peer data and the nascent, unproven commercial deployment models across the broader sector. Investors should treat this range as provisional pending materialization of revenue traction or material changes in the comparable set.
